samira.v: Quick question 
I'm on a 6-month secondment in Germany and my partner and I just had a baby there. Can I add the baby to Redwood benefits while I'm on local payroll?

maria.peopleops: Congrats Samira! You can request a QLE to add the child, but cross-border payroll and carrier rules can complicate effective dates and billing. Two things to decide first: you vs partner as primary insurer, and whether the carrier accepts a foreign birth cert + translation.

samira.v: I'm still on Redwood benefits but getting paid through our Germany entity. The child's birth cert is German (PDF). Will that be accepted?

maria.peopleops: Usually yes, carriers accept foreign certificates if accompanied by an English translation. An apostille or certified translation speeds processing. Also let us know if the child has a German health ID (eGK) or is immediately covered under partner's local plan 1; that affects coordination.

samira.v: Partner's employer offers local coverage that started at birth. If I add the child here, how do we decide primary?

maria.peopleops: COB rules still apply. If both parents have coverage, most US carriers use the birthday rule for parents. However, if partner's local plan is primary by local law or by contract, claims for EU providers may be routed there first. We'll coordinate with the broker to confirm for our carrier.

ben.payroll: From payroll side: when you're paid on local payroll, deductions for US benefits can be tricky. If the carrier sets an effective date, we may need to gross-up or bill you locally depending on tax rules. We can estimate the deduction and whether an after-the-fact adjustment is required.

samira.v: OK. What's the doc checklist and how do I submit?

maria.peopleops: Docs we typically need: German birth certificate PDF, certified English translation (or notarized), proof of residency (utility or registration), and partner's insurer details if dual coverage. Upload via People Ops portal > Benefits > QLE uploads or email benefits@redwood.com with subject: "QLE: Add dependent - international birth - <Samira V>". benefits-bot will ack.

benefits-bot: Received. If you upload now, case #RB-2338 created. Carrier verification may take 5-12 business days due to cross-border checks.

samira.v: Timeline is tight 
I have a pediatric visit in 7 days. Can we get coverage confirmed fast?

maria.peopleops: If it's urgent, DM me the provider name and appointment date; we can request a predetermination/coverage letter from the carrier and ask the broker to expedite. Note: EU providers may still bill the local insurer first.

liaison-emea: Quick add 
If you need translated docs, the local HR team can point you to certified translators and the municipal "Anmeldung" or Geburtsurkunde attestation services. Happy to connect you to them.

samira.v: Thanks everyone  I'll upload the cert + translation and include partner insurer details. Please ping me if carrier needs anything else.

maria.peopleops: Sounds good. Ping this thread after upload and we'll track the case and loop payroll for the deduction estimate. :thumbsup:
